elements.texte:
[cheerful] The products come 3 by 3: one query each time “See more” is tapped.

It’s useful for showing long lists, without loading everything at once.

It’s used first on websites and in apps…

…but also in business software, for example to browse customers or invoices in groups of 20.

With each click on “Next”, offset moves forward by 20: invoices 21 to 40, then 41 to 60.

In dashboards, to show only the last 5 orders.

When an order comes in, it goes to the top of the list, and the oldest one drops off.

In APIs, to send back part of the results with each request.

The app asks for page 2: the server runs limit 3 offset 3 and sends back 3 products.

And in processing scripts, to get data in batches.

The script exports 2,000 orders, 500 by 500: offset moves forward by 500 with each batch.
elements.apres: Pour finir, voici les trois idées à retenir.
